links.reason: The Nalli link is real: 238 names him with இரப்போர்க்கு இழை அணி நெடுந்தேர் களிறொடு ... மழைசுரந் தன்ன ஈகை, and 150 shows a gift of chain and bracelet given while he withholds his name (பேரும் சொல்லான்). But in 238 Nalli only lends his slope's fragrance to her forehead, and the claim that the akam poet 'assumes hearers who knew stories like 150' cannot be checked from either poem.

The image is distinctive and the same in both: 227 வித்துஅட்டு உண்டனை and 230 வீழ்குடி உழவன் வித்து உண்டாஅங்கு, each arguing that Death ate the king who fed it enemies (227 நின் வாடுபசி அருந்திய; 230 நேரார் பல்லுயிர் பருகி ஆர்குவை). Two poets on two kings with one conceit supports the claim of a recognised kaiyarunilai move.

The phrase is shared but its sense differs. In 3, பின்நின்று துரக்கும் நெஞ்சம் is a heart pushing him from behind. In 19, பின்நின்று ஒழியச் சூழ்ந்தனை is a heart that lags behind and stays back. Two uses do not make a 'fixed paalai figure', and the closing claim about where the debate happens is grander than the Tamil.

The pairing works: 218 says gems from far apart (இடைபடச் சேய ஆயினும்) meet in one jewel, and the Naladiyar says the ambal and kuvalai born in one pool (ஒருநீர்ப் பிறந்து) stay unequal, so near versus far is a real complementary contrast. But neither verse extends the other. Both claim that nature, not place, decides fellowship, so the right type is agrees.

A real shared custom: 290 asks இவற்குஈந்து உண்மதி கள்ளே, and 298 complains of கலங்கல் given while the king drinks the தேறல். But 298 does not limit 290, and the 'order of dying' link rests on reading நீ முந்து என்னானே as a denial of the vanguard, in a verse the marker flags as uncertain. 290 ties the cup to shielding (மறைக்குவன் ... வேலே), not to going first.

The verbal echo is exact and specific: பேதைக்கு அமர்த்தன கண் against 390 அமர்த்தனள் நோக்கி ... பல்மாண் பேதைக்கு. The poem gives the glare a cause, the man's joke about her body's salt and his blocking her (சிறிய விலங்கினமாக; யாரீரோ எம் விலங்கியீஇர்), and ends it in மூரல் முறுவல். The couplet does not have that.

Both concern a king's demand on his subjects. The Kural casts it as a spear-holder's 'hand it over' (வேலொடு நின்றான் இடுவென்றது), while 184 argues from yield and waste: an elephant loose in the field (யானை புக்க புலம்போல) leaves the king himself unfed (தானும் உண்ணான்). The moral ground versus the prudential ground is a real and specific difference.

Both speak of poverty and kin, but they make different claims. 151's maxim is that the poor cannot support dependants or laugh with kin (நகுதல் ஆற்றார் நல்கூர்ந்தோர்), while 1047 says a poverty unjoined to virtue (அறஞ்சாரா நல்குரவு) makes even a mother see one as a stranger. So the Kural does not state 'the claim the hero uses', and the link rests on the shared topic.

The echo is real: 58 நல்ல போலவும் நயவ போலவும் ... ஏதில் மாக்கள் பொதுமொழி, against 826 நட்டார்போல் நல்லவை சொல்லினும். But the note misses the difference: the Kural is confident such words are soon seen through (ஒல்லை உணரப்படும), whereas 58 warns the kings precisely because they may not be. 'Already a matter of statecraft' adds nothing, since the Kural chapter is itself statecraft.

Kanaiyan is named in both (386 நற்போர்க் கணையன் நாணியாங்கு; 44 கணையன் அகப்பட), a real puram name in two akam poems. But in 44 he is only a captured chief in a list, not a figure of shame, so two mentions do not show 'a byword for humiliation'. Only 386 uses his shame as the measure of the wife's.

The opening plea matches: செல்வீர் வருவீர் ஆகுதல் உரைமின் மன்னோ against செல்லாமை உண்டேல் எனக்குரை ... வல்வரவு. But the teaches misreads the lizard: lines 16 to 19 (பல்லி சிறிய தெற்றுவதாயின் ... உயர்ந்தோர் ஆயினும் நின்றாங்குப் பெயரும்) say that at an ill omen even the great turn back. That is an argument for not setting out, which fits the thurai (செலவு அழுங்க), and not a point about whether a return can be promised.
links.text_issue: Lines 4 to 8 and line 20 (சென்றோர் மன்னென இருக்கிற் போர்க்கே) are obscure as printed.

links.reason: Minjili's war in both Paranar poems is a real puram link, and 181 has birds massing to hide the sun when Aay Eyinan falls. But in 142, புள்ளிற்கு ஏமம் ஆகிய stands between வாய்மொழி மிஞிலி and அதிகற் கொன்று and can describe Minjili rather than Athikan. The two-heroes-one-legend conclusion turns on a construction the Tamil does not fix, and nothing here limits anything, so qualifies is the wrong type.

The phrase கருங்கைக் கொல்லன் is shared. In 180 the smith forges the spear that will feed bards (திருந்திலை நெடுவேல் வடித்திசின்), but in 170 the anvil (உலைக்கல் அன்ன) belongs only to the hardness shown to foes, set against gentleness to seekers (நசைவர்க்கு மென்மை). So the forge does not 'stand in both poems for the link between fighting and giving'. The shared phrase looks like a stock epithet.

The two mullai homes share real detail: varagu (394 வரகின்; 384 கவைக்கதிர் வரகின் சீறூர்), a hare, and a meal or guest. The friend's நின் மனையோள் does look forward to the wife who receives a guest (விருந்தேர் பெற்றனள்). But this is the conventional path from kalavu to karpu across two poems, so the pairing shows the thinai convention more than anything new.

On the plain reading the conflict is real, and even the verb is shared. 316 honours as அவன் எம் இறைவன் the lord who sleeps drunk (கள்ளின் வாழ்த்தி ... அனந்தர்த் துஞ்சுவோனே), while 926 says sleepers are as the dead (துஞ்சினார் செத்தாரின் வேறல்லர்) and drinkers eat poison. 'Heroic ideal' slightly overstates it, since what 316 celebrates is the drinker's generosity, but the opposition holds.

314 does join the house and the battle in one man: மனைக்கு விளக்காகிய ... குடியும் மன்னுந் தானே ... சிறையும் தானே. That literalises the Kural's comparison (அமரகத்து வன்கண்ணர் போலத் தமரகத்தும்). The claim that the couplet's figure 'grew from' this social fact is a historical guess the verses cannot support.

Evvi's death links the two, and 115 uses the bards' gesture (பாணர் கைதொழு மரபின் முன் பரித்துஇடூஉப் பழிச்சிய வள்உயிர் வணர்மருப்பு) as an image for konrai pods. But 233 has no harp image, so there is no shared image. 115 alone already calls the gesture a மரபு, so the pairing adds only that both poems mourn Evvi.

The name is shared (177 கழற்கால் பண்ணன் காவிரி வடவயின்; 173 names Pannan only in its text and the colophon gives Sirukudi). But 177 praises Pannan as a warrior whose spear routed elephants (வென்வேல் ... யானை மண்டுஅமர் ஒழித்த), not as a feeder. So 'a patron's renown for feeding becomes a measure of beauty' does not match the akam poem.

Both give love-sickness a plant that gossip makes grow: 1147 ஊரவர் கெளவை எருவாக ... நீளும்இந் நோய், and 273 a tree with அம்பல் for branches and அலர் for buds (ஊரோர் எடுத்த அம்பல் அம்சினை ... அலர்அரும்பு ஊழ்ப்பவும்). The teaches names the real difference: gossip is manure from outside in the Kural but part of the plant itself in the poem. 'Seed' should be read as logical, not historical.

The taunt of youth is a real echo: 72 இளையன் இவன் and 78 பொருநனும் இளையன். But 78 names no king (என்ஐ only; patron blank), so the claim that it tells the sequel of Neduncheliyan's vow rests on an identification that neither the poem nor its colophon makes.

The verses have different concerns. Kural 221 is about the receiver's want (வறியார்க்கு) and the absence of return (குறியெதிர்ப்பை), whereas 106 is about the receiver's worth: Pari gives even to மடவர் மெல்லியர், as gods accept the erukkam that is நல்லவும் தீயவும் அல்ல. The teaches merges non-discrimination into non-reciprocity.

The smallest request is the same, asking for water: 154 சின்னீர் வினவுவர் and 1066 ஆவிற்கு நீரென்று இரப்பினும். The poet makes it the natural image for seeking the generous, the Kural the extreme of degradation. The teaches honestly notes that 154 concedes ஈயென இரத்தலோ அரிதே, so the opposition is stated on its defensible ground.

The phrase பொய்யா விளக்கு is shared, but 299 does not name truth in the couplet, and the two verses speak in different domains, wealth in 753 and the worthy man's light in 299. Incompatibility therefore needs the chapter context. 'Compete for one title' only restates the shared phrase.

Mullur and a fame formula are shared (123 தொலையா நல்லிசை ... முள்ளூர்; 209 முள்ளூர் மன்னன் ... காரி செல்லா நல்லிசை). But in 209, செல்லா நல்லிசை நிறுத்த வல்வில் ஓரி can describe Ori rather than Kari. The heroine's beauty is measured by the Kolli பாவை, not by Kari's fame, so the teaches misdescribes the akam use.

The whole line கள்ளி போகிய களரியம் பறந்தலை is identical (225 l.7, 237 l.13) in two kaiyarunilai poems on different patrons, which shows a shared formula. What each sets on that ground differs as stated: an army's strength in 225 (ஆற்றல் என்பதன் தோற்றம்) and the young hero's death amid grieving suppliants in 237.

Both tie a good death to a king's response. But 307 says only வெஞ்சின யானை வேந்தனும் ... இக்களத்து எஞ்சலின் சிறந்தது பிறிதொன்று இல், and nothing marks this king as the enemy. The teaches ('did not depend on whose side mourned') rests on that unsupported reading, and the king's words are admiration, not the tears of K780.
links.text_issue: Lines 13 and 14 (பண் கொளற்கு அருமை நோக்கி, நெஞ்சற வீழ்ந்த புரைமையோனே) are obscure, and who falls is unclear.

links.reason: Irungo Venman in 36's list of seven fallen at Alankanam may be of the house that 202's colophon calls இருங்கோவேள, but 202's text names only புலிகடி மாஅல். The teaches also calls 36's speaker the 'akam friend', though the colophon gives தலைமகள் புலந்து சொல்லியது, and the claim that Kapilar 'does not foresee' the defeat assumes a chronology neither poem gives.

The same event is told in nearly the same words: அன்னி குறுக்கைப் பறந்தலைத் திதியன் தொல்நிலை முழுமுதல் துமியப் பண்ணிய ... புன்னை. 45 uses it for noise (வயிரியர் இன்இசை ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிதே) and 145 for ruin (புன்னை போலக் கடுநவைப் படீஇயர் ... கையே). One puram event serving two different measures is a specific, verifiable lesson.

There is a real opposition between the Kural's curse on living by asking (இரந்தும் உயிர்வாழ்தல் வேண்டின்) and the parisil life. But 'hereditary office' rests on one reading of குடிமுறை பாடி, which can as well mean singing house by house. The poem itself calls the life wretched (பழங்கண் வாழ்க்கை), so it does not present asking as a calling against the Kural.
links.text_issue: Line 22 has a gap, and line 2 has an edition variant.

links.reason: A distinctive working image is shared: 60 ஆரைச் சாகாட்டு ஆழ்ச்சி போக்கும் உரனுடை நோன்பகட்டு and 140 மாமூதள்ளல் அழுந்திய சாகாட்டு எவ்வந் தீர வாங்குந் தந்தை கைபூண் பகட்டின் வருந்தி. The puram poet takes the ox's strength for the king, the akam lover its strain (வருந்தி வெய்ய உயிர்க்கும்), which is accurately stated.

Both use rain for giving. The Kural keeps the side that asks no return (கைம்மாறு வேண்டா கடப்பாடு மாரிமாட்டு), while 142 adds the waste, rain that feeds salt land (உறுமிடத்து உதவாது உவர்நிலம் ஊட்டியும்), and names Pekan's கொடைமடம். This is a genuine qualification of the figure.

These are the two Rama allusions in the poems: monkeys decked in Sita's dropped jewels (378 நிலஞ்சேர் மதர் அணி கண்ட குரங்கின் ... கிளை) and the banyan silenced for Rama's counsel (70 இராமன் அருமறைக்கு அவித்த பல்வீழ் ஆலம்). Each is a by-way of the story used as a simile for a crowd, the bard's kin and the clamorous town. The claim about detailed knowledge of the story is fair.

The bard in 394 is poor (இரும்பேர் ஒக்கல் பெரும்புலம்பு), so the elephants are given to one in want and meet Kural 221's test (வறியார்க்கு). The claim that the Kural 'would hardly count' this as ஈகை is therefore unfounded. 394's point is the gift's excess in a mock complaint, which Kural 221 does not address.

The Kosar are named in both: 283 வலம்புரி கோசர் அவைக்களத்தானும் and 262 ஊர்முது கோசர் who blinded the father. Both cast them as a judging body. But 283 is a gapped fragment that gives no context for the council, and in 262 the akam use is Anni Minjili's joy at revenge, not the Kosar's council cited as a wrong.
links.text_issue: Purananuru 283 lines 7 and 12 have gaps, and line 3 has an edition variant.

links.reason: The conditional formula is a real echo: 95 உண்டாயின் பதம் கொடுத்து இல்லாயின் உடன் உண்ணும் against 315 உடையன் ஆயின் உண்ணவும் வல்லன். But 315 does not address what Anji does in want: its point is giving beyond what he owes (கடவர் மீதும்) and latent force (the fire-drill). So 'both poems answer the same question' is untrue of 315.

The line விண்தோய் சிமைய விறல்வரைக் கவாஅன் is identical (179 l.1, 151 l.2). In 151 it belongs to the generous lord's hill (கிழவன்), and in 179 it opens the waste of fire and thirst the friend warns of. The claim that the setting decides the line's value is shown by the pair.

Both name a king's levy as begging: 75 குடிபுரவு இரக்கும் and 552 கோலொடு நின்றான் இரவு. 75 adds what the Kural lacks, the petty heir's valuing of rule (எய்தினம் சிறப்பு) against the worthy man for whom it is light as dry kidai (வெண்கிடை ... வறல் போல ... நொய்து).

The earth-and-water figure is shared in the context of sulking. 1323 makes the bond (நிலத்தொடு நீரியைந் தன்னார்) the reason புலத்தல் is sweet, while in 26 the man melts like ploughed red earth taking rain (பலஉழு செஞ்செய் மண்போல் நெகிழ்ந்து), which ends her புலத்தல் (புலத்தல் கூடுமோ). The same image works for the quarrel in the Kural and against it in the poem.

The exclamation is a real shared formula: உண்டால் அம்ம இவ்வுலகம் and இன்னாது அம்ம இவ் வுலகம். But the claims are not opposite: one says why the world endures, the other that it is harsh. 182 does not 'turn it to action', since it is a description of the selfless, so the 'anthology arguing with itself' is overdrawn.

Two kuthirai maram poems by different poets share the frame ___ச் செகுக்கும் காளை, with the slot filled differently: நோக்கினர்ச் in 302 and எள்ளுநர்ச் in 303. The claim of a stock epithet with a variable slot follows directly from the Tamil.

27 reports as hearsay (என்ப ... எனக் கேட்பல்) that those whom poets praise reach a sky-car, and 234 ties earthly fame (நிலவரை நீள்புகழ்) to the gods' world. The premise link is real. But 234 is elliptical and turns on who the புலவர் are, a sense the couplet does not fix, so the 'premise the Kural leaves out' is one reading.

The echo is exact (செற்றார்பின் செல்லா against இகழ்வார்பின் சென்று). But 1255 grants the honour and only says the love-sick cannot know it (காமநோய் உற்றார் அறிவதொன்று அன்று). As the teaches itself says, that limits 966 rather than contradicting it.

Two different poets press Kumanan with the child at the milkless breast: 164 பாஅல் இன்மையின் ... வறுமுலை சுவைத்தொறும் அழூஉம் and 160 பாலில் வறுமுலைசுவைத்தனன்பெறாஅன். Both are பரிசில் கடாநிலை. The claim of a set argument of the plea, not a private report, is well supported.
links.text_issue: Purananuru 160 has misprint candidates at lines 6, 10, 14 and 21, which do not affect the breast image.

poems.note: களவன் ஆக (line 2) is hard; the male snail joining its mate in the full pond answers to the man bathing with the woman he desires, and the pond's openness to the public bathing.

iraicchi.act: kills a stag to end the hunger of its mate (பிணவின் உறுபசி களைஇயர்)
iraicchi.sense: The man who has asked her to come will provide for her on the waste road as the dog provides for its mate.

poems.note: The anril's call is a sound only; no act ties it to the lovers.
The waves that wreck the girls' sand houses fit the confinement (இல்வயிற் செறித்தமை), but மூத்தோர் அன்ன openly joins them to elders.
The buffalo that goes out at dawn and grazes the fresh neythal flower answers to the man who enjoys her and leaves at daybreak without marrying.
The wounded tusker that overcame the tiger and comforts its herd answers to the hero braving the night path, and the herd's relief (ஏமார்ப்ப) to the women's anxious waiting.

iraicchi.act: breaks its tusk goring a dry maraa tree to feed its mate in the hard summer (இன்றுணை ஆர ... ஊட்ட)
iraicchi.sense: The waste would not be hard for the man if he took the girl and cared for her on the road, as the elephant does its mate.

iraicchi.act: the female monkey frolics with her mate, snatching jack fruit in his hills
iraicchi.sense: In his own land the pair are together, as the lovers should be, while he who swore has left her alone.

poems.note: The guarding of new paddy from an old cow suggests the guarded girl, but no second correspondence is clear.

iraicchi.act: the hen apart from its cock suffers through the night in the nest
iraicchi.sense: She, sleepless (துஞ்சாக் கண்ணள்), suffers apart from him as the hen does, while he thinks only of his own town.

iraicchi.act: the bull elephant, fearing the yaali, embraces its trembling pregnant mate with its trunk
iraicchi.sense: The man should have stayed to hold and protect her through the cold season, as the bull does its mate.

iraicchi.act: runs after the mirage taking it for water (ஆவி ... நீரென நசைஇ)
iraicchi.sense: The heart that drives him after wealth chases an illusion and would leave her for nothing.

poems.note: மா is unspecific (animal or deer), but the act is clear.
The colophon's தலைமகற்குத் தலைமகன் is probably a misprint for தலைமகள்.
